title: Qonclave check-in exchange
description: The single round trip a duty-cycled device performs per wake. A device that wakes for 200 ms cannot afford separate calls to post events, fetch commands, sync config, and sync time — radio-on time is the battery budget, so round trips are the metric that matters, not bytes. The uplink carries everything the device has to say; the downlink carries everything the hub has been holding for it since the last contact. MANDATORY for the `minimal` profile, RECOMMENDED for `constrained`, unused by `full`.

wake_counter.description: Monotonic wake count. Doubles as a replay guard: a hub MUST reject a check-in whose wake_counter is not greater than the last one it accepted from this node.

events.description: Observations accumulated since last contact — normally one, but a device that failed to reach the hub on previous wakes drains its spool here.

config_version.description: Version of the config the device currently holds. The hub returns a delta only when this is stale, so an unchanged config costs zero downlink bytes.

ack.description: command_ids delivered in a previous check-in that the device has now executed. Until a command is acked the hub MUST keep it in the mailbox, so a device that dies mid-wake retries next cycle.

grant.description: Present only when checking in with a hub that did not commission this device. Omitted in the normal home-hub case.

server_time.description: Authoritative time. This is how a device with a drifted or unset RTC learns what time it is, and how relative_time on its events gets anchored.

accepted.description: event_ids the hub durably accepted. Anything absent MUST be retained in the device spool and retried next wake.

commands.description: Mailbox drain: commands queued since last contact, expired ones already removed. VISION.md's asynchronous sleep-queue.

config.description: Config delta, present only if the device's config_version was stale.

next_checkin_s.description: How long the hub would like the device to sleep before checking in again. Advisory — the device owns its own power budget and MAY ignore it. This is how a hub applies backpressure to a fleet without an always-on control channel.
